taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit: a shrub (FEIS, Anderson 2001).

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: FEIS species review, Krameria erecta (Griffith 1991): "a native, long-lived, deciduous, perennial shrub that grows from 12 to 24 inches (30-60 cm) tall".

traits.height_max_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: 1 m at most; the Range Plant Handbook (p. B88) gives 1 to 2 feet.

traits.life_span.note: FEIS species review, Krameria erecta (Griffith 1991): "a native, long-lived, deciduous, perennial shrub".

traits.woodiness.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 422), Krameria parvifolia: a woody, straggling shrub with rigid branchlets.

traits.leaf_habit.note: FEIS species review, Krameria erecta (Griffith 1991): "deciduous"; it "retains its leaves for up to 2 months longer in the fall" than its neighbours.

traits.rosette.note: FEIS species review, Krameria erecta (Griffith 1991): "densely branched", leafy along the twigs: no rosette.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: FEIS species review, Krameria erecta (Griffith 1991): "The leaves are alternate and pubescent".

traits.leaf_division.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 627, Krameria glandulosa: leaves narrowly linear, simple.

traits.leaf_incision.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 627, Krameria glandulosa: leaves narrowly linear, entire.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 627, Krameria glandulosa: leaves 5-10 mm. long (K. imparata, p. 628: 2-12 mm).

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 627, Krameria glandulosa: leaves narrowly linear, less than 1 mm. wide.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Range Plant Handbook (1937) p. B88, Range ratany: leaves linear, silky.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 627, Krameria glandulosa: leaves narrowly linear, entire.

traits.leaf_hairs.note: Range Plant Handbook (1937) p. B88, Range ratany: leaves silky; Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 422): harshly strigose.

traits.inflorescence.note: Flowers borne singly in the axils along the twigs, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 162433107, 156295305, 207803442, 194547216, 112063786, 9400976, 338806796, 406882897): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.flowering_position.note: Flowers in the leaf axils, along the twigs, set by hand from iNaturalist photos (observations 162433107, 156295305, 207803442, 194547216, 112063786, 9400976, 338806796, 406882897): the sources read give no count or measure.

traits.flower_size_m.note: Range Plant Handbook (1937) p. B88, Range ratany: flowers about 3/4 inch across, purplish.

traits.flower_colour.note: FEIS species review, Krameria erecta (Griffith 1991): "flowers are irregular and purple in color"; sRGB by eye from the photos (magenta-purple sepals).

traits.flower_merosity.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 421), Krameria: petals 5, smaller than the sepals.

traits.flower_symmetry.note: FEIS species review, Krameria erecta (Griffith 1991): "flowers are irregular".

traits.sepal_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 628, Krameria imparata: sepals 6-11 mm. long.

traits.petal_length_m.note: FNA vol. 12 (eFloras), Krameria erecta: "secretory petals pink, 2–3 mm … petaloid petals 4–6 mm"; the petaloid petals, the larger and showy pair, set the range, the secretory ones kept as the rare low.

traits.stamens.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 421), Krameria: stamens 3 or 4; 4 here, as in the photos' flowers.

traits.fruit_type.note: FEIS species review, Krameria erecta (Griffith 1991): "the fruit is globose, indehiscent, thick walled, and spiny": a nut-like bur.

traits.fruit_shape.note: FEIS species review, Krameria erecta (Griffith 1991): "the fruit is globose".

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Abrams vol. 2 (1944) p. 627, Krameria glandulosa: fruit 6-7 mm. in diameter.

traits.fruit_armature.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 422), Krameria parvifolia: fruit spines barbed below the apex (Abrams 1944 p. 628: prickles barbed on the sides).

traits.fruit_colour_ripe.note: Range Plant Handbook (1937) p. B88, Range ratany: burlike fruit with purple barbed spines; sRGB by eye from the photos.

traits.flowering_months.note: FNA vol. 12 (eFloras), Krameria erecta: "Flowering Mar–Oct"; Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 422), Krameria parvifolia: "5,000 feet or lower, April to October". FEIS (Griffith 1991) adds that in wet years it flowers "twice, in the spring and again in the fall".

traits.fruiting_months.note: FEIS species review, Krameria erecta (Griffith 1991): fruiting on May 22, about 17 days after flowering (May 5); with flowers from March to October (FNA), fruits April to October.

traits.elevation_min_m.note: FEIS species review, Krameria erecta (Griffith 1991): "generally grows at elevations ranging from 500 to 5,000 feet (150-1,500 m)".

traits.elevation_max_m.note: FEIS species review, Krameria erecta (Griffith 1991): "generally grows at elevations ranging from 500 to 5,000 feet (150-1,500 m)"; Kearney and Peebles (1942, p. 422): 5,000 feet or lower.

traits.light.note: FEIS species review, Krameria erecta (Griffith 1991): "commonly occurs in the understory of catclaw acacia", Joshua tree and juniper, and in the open: sun to part shade.

traits.moisture.note: FEIS species review, Krameria erecta (Griffith 1991): "drought resistant"; "The annual precipitation is 8 to 25 inches (20-65 cm)".

appearance.note: By eye, from the photos the traits cite: a low, dense, intricately branched grey shrub with silky grey-green linear leaves and scattered magenta-purple flowers, then round burs with purple barbed spines. Colours set by eye were written as screen (sRGB) shades; they are read as the linear light a colour field holds, and bark and foliage follow the stated colour traits by rule (2026-10-19).

generator.params.note: Set by hand for range ratany from its sources and the photos the traits cite, on the template of snowbrush ceanothus (ceanothus-velutinus); the rest of its growth comes from the library's rules for the form. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 0.45 m tall at 10 years in the open, within its sources' range, as it grows on a Sonoran Desert bajada. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

sources.title: Project After contributors: hand-set species values
sources.licence: project contribution under the repository's terms

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added for the Saguaro desert scene (west bajada, Tucson Mountain District, 2026-10-19): sizes and forms from FEIS, Kearney and Peebles (1942) and Abrams, counts and colours from iNaturalist photos, drawing values from the library's rules for the form.
